questions.q: Select the option that changes the degree of comparison in the given sentence from superlative to positive without changing the meaning of the sentence.
o: Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls of the colony.
Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja.
questions.s:
Answer: No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.

Explanation:

  • The original sentence uses the superlative form: "the tallest girl."

  • The correct positive degree form that keeps the same meaning is:
    "No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja."

  • This compares Kalpana’s height with others without using the superlative.

Other options:

  • "Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls" – incorrect grammar

  • "Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja" – opposite meaning

  • "No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja" – incorrect grammar

Correct sentence:
"No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja."

questions.q: This is (a) / the most worst (b) / day of my life. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Worst' is superlative, so 'most' is incorrect. Correct form is 'the worst.' Answer: (b). 'Worst' superlative hai, 'most' galat hai. Sahi form hai 'the worst.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: What is the / price of this / fancy dress pink?
questions.s:
Adjectives typically come before the noun they modify.
The color of the dress, 'pink', is an adjective and it should come before the noun 'dress'.
Correct form : "What is the price of this fancy pink dress?”

questions.q: The watermelon tasted sweetly and refreshing on a hot summer day.
o: The watermelon tasted sweetly
on a hot summer day.
questions.s:
Generally, verbs are modified by adverbs. But verbs of sensation (seem, look, appear, feel, taste, sound, and smell) and ‘be’, ‘become’, ‘turn’, ‘get’, ‘grow’, ‘keep’, ‘make’, and ‘prove’ are followed by an adjective and not an adverb.

According to the given rule, the correct option is (b) "The watermelon tasted sweetly."

So, the error lies in using "sweetly" as an adverb instead of using the adjective "sweet" to modify the verb "tasted."

The correct sentence should be: "The watermelon tasted sweet and refreshing on a hot summer day."

questions.s: Adjective order: "a beautiful red balloon".

questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He was not able to give many time to his research.
questions.s:
The correct answer is- many time.

Key Points

  • ​An adjective is any member of a class of words that modify nouns and pronouns.
  • ​Let's have a look at the meanings of the given adjectives:
    • Much- a great amount or quantity of
    • Some- an unspecified amount or number of
    • Many- a large number of
  • The adjective 'much' is used with uncountable nouns, whereas 'many' is used with plural countable nouns.
  • Since the noun 'time' is an uncountable noun, the adjective 'much' is an appropriate choice.
     

Correct Sentence: He was not able to give much time to his research. 

Additional Information  

  • ​The following adjectives are always followed by 'to' and not 'than':
    • Junior, senior, superior, inferior, prior, prefer/preferable, anterior, posterior.
  • For example:
    • My sister is junior than me.
    • My sister is junior to me.
